dialect.detail: IBM mainframe style with VSAM KSDS indexed file, RECORDING MODE F, COMP-3, RETURN-CODE special register, and FUNCTION NUMVAL usage consistent with IBM Enterprise COBOL
evidence: ORGANIZATION INDEXED ACCESS RANDOM RECORD ACCT-KEY STATUS

purpose.domain_detail: Account record lookup: reads an index file of account IDs and currency codes, performs random reads against a VSAM KSDS account master file, and writes matched records to a print output file
purpose.summary: COBHW03 reads sequential index records containing account ID and currency code, uses them as keys to randomly access a VSAM indexed account master file, and writes matching account details (ID, currency, name, surname) to a print output file. Invalid key conditions are reported via DISPLAY.

notable_features: VSAM KSDS indexed file with ORGANIZATION INDEXED and RANDOM access
RECORDING MODE F on sequential files
RETURN-CODE special register used for error propagation
88-level condition names for file status codes including 97
verdict.notes: The AUTHOR field names an individual (Mert Musa TEMEL) and the program name COBHW03 suggests a homework assignment (HW=homework, 03=third exercise). Logic is functional but has a minor bug: the OPEN OUTPUT PRINT-LINE status check tests ACCT-ST instead of PRT-ST. No COPY statements or CALLs. Dialect is likely IBM mainframe based on VSAM and RECORDING MODE F but could also compile under GnuCOBOL.
